_comment: Who a practice is for — the dimension the directory has never held.
Every term carries a `test`: the specific, checkable thing that must be
true of a practice's own published material before the term may be
applied. These are deliberately narrow. An audience term is Oria Haven
asserting something about a named business, so the bar is what they say
about themselves, not what we infer from a category.
Nothing here describes an outcome. 'Pregnancy' means the practice
publishes services for pregnant clients — never that anything is good
for pregnancy. Same rule as the listings, the FAQs and the articles.
Absence is not a negative. A listing without `beginners` means nobody
has checked, not that beginners are unwelcome, and no page may phrase
it as the latter. See Audience\coverage().

audiences.name: Beginner friendly
audiences.question: Do you run anything specifically for people who have never done this before?
audiences.test: Publishes a beginners' class or course, or a 'new here, start with this' page, or states plainly that classes suit all levels or need no experience. An intro offer on its own does not count — that is a discount on the first visit, not a statement about who the class suits.

audiences.name: Seniors
audiences.question: Do you run anything specifically for older adults?
audiences.test: Publishes a class, session or programme named for seniors, older adults or an age band above 60.

audiences.name: Pregnancy and postnatal
audiences.question: Do you offer sessions for clients who are pregnant or recently gave birth?
audiences.test: Publishes prenatal, pregnancy, antenatal, postnatal or postpartum services. Describes who the service is for — never what it does.

audiences.name: Children and teens
audiences.question: Do you see clients under 18?
audiences.test: Publishes services for children, kids, teens or a named under-18 age range.

audiences.name: Families
audiences.question: Do you run sessions a family attends together?
audiences.test: Publishes a session or programme families attend together, rather than simply seeing people of several ages separately.

audiences.name: Couples
audiences.question: Do you offer sessions for two people together?
audiences.test: Publishes a couples, partner or two-person session.

audiences.name: Women's sessions
audiences.question: Do you run anything for women only?
audiences.test: Publishes a women-only class, circle, clinic or practitioner. Not simply that most clients are women.

audiences.name: Men's sessions
audiences.question: Do you run anything for men only?
audiences.test: Publishes a men-only class, group or programme.

audiences.name: Workplaces
audiences.question: Do you work with employers or teams?
audiences.test: Publishes a corporate, workplace or team offering, on site or otherwise.

audiences.name: Step-free access
audiences.question: Can someone reach your space without stairs?
audiences.test: States step-free, ground-floor, lift or wheelchair access to the space itself. Never inferred from a photograph.

audiences.name: Drop-in welcome
audiences.question: Can someone come once without signing up to a term or membership?
audiences.test: Publishes casual, drop-in or single-class attendance without a term, course or membership commitment.
